2963ff04d6df04ac: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The move by MCA to walk out of an event to unveil Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates for the 16th Melaka state election Saturday night has raised questions regarding the sincerity of its coalition partner, Umno, in their political cooperation.

Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said this situation also casts doubt on the foundation of BN’s political alliances with other parties, questioning whether they are built on principles and trust, or merely on political interests and power.
“If MCA, a long-standing BN component party, feels disrespected, what does this mean for other parties that have entered into cooperation with BN?

“Is this cooperation based on principles and trust, or is it driven solely by political interests and power?” asked Chang, who also serves as the Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, in a statement tonight.
Meanwhile, PKR Women’s Wing vice chief Loh Ker Chean remarked that the MCA should have long been aware of Umno’s style of poor treatment toward its component parties.

Loh noted that the situation stands in contrast to Pakatan Harapan (PH), where Keadilan as a founding party of the coalition does not adopt a ‘big brother’ mentality or bully other parties, as is allegedly the case within BN.
“PMX (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) has always been consultative and inclusive, even when dealing with smaller parties such as UPKO (United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation) in the past.”
“Therefore, PH is stronger and more stable in governing the country,” she said.
Meanwhile, Keadilan Youth (AMK) information chief, Danish Hairudin, said MCA’s actions indicate the party is beginning to realise that it is not respected by Umno, its own coalition partner.
He alleged that Umno is so preoccupied with the prospect of short-term political gains through its cooperation with PAS that it has completely disregarded both MCA and MIC.
“This also raises the question of whether any coalition government involving Umno and PAS would simply cast aside the voices and interests of minority groups.”
“The reality is that, collectively, MCA and MIC hold only three seats in the Dewan Rakyat and do not occupy any ministerial positions,” he said.

Earlier, MCA announced that it would not recognise any of its party members named as candidates by BN for the Melaka state election if such nominations were made without the approval of its top leadership.

MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong reportedly said that announcing candidates without consultation or the party’s consent is unacceptable, especially given allegations that seats previously contested by MCA have been handed over to other parties.

Meanwhile, BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, speaking after officiating the Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge Run 2026 in Bagan Datuk, Perak, said MCA’s grievances regarding the announcement of BN candidates for the Melaka state election would be discussed and resolved collectively before October 31.

The issue arose after Wee and the MCA leadership walked out of the event last night prior to the BN chairman’s keynote address and the announcement of candidates and subsequently held a press conference outside the venue. — Bernama

55ef0b64e321e458: RIO DE JANEIRO (Brazil), Oct 26— Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback yesterday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round.
The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied all projections to win an unprecedented fourth term at the helm of Latin America’s largest country.

According to official results, he won 51.75 per cen tof the votes to 48.25 per cent for Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who had entered election day confident with his lead in the polls.
With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.

After a campaign marred by scandal and mud-slinging, yesterday’s vote plunged into chaos after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extending voting by two hours, at the request of Lula who said buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting.
Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some parts of the country due to heavy rains, but his camp lashed out at the country-wide extension.
“Either we win. Or we win. Consider yourself warned,” pro-Bolsonaro lawmaker Nikolas Ferreira wrote on X as the votes streamed in.
The bitter campaign laid bare the deep divisions in the country of over 200 million people.
“It’s a disgrace. We’ve never had anything like this in Brazil, and now they’ve come up with the idea of extending the election period by two hours,” said Aurelio Junior, 45, a dentist in Brasilia.
Jacqueline Maria Lima de Franca, 34, a business owner in Rio de Janeiro backing Lula said it was “more than fair…everyone should have the right to vote, and that was being neglected.”
Lula rises from the ashes, again
Lula, a defining figure in Brazilian politics over four decades, was blindsided after his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro.

The left swung into action with massive rallies declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro,” where protesters recalled the former president’s chaotic handling of the Covid pandemic, devastation of the Amazon rainforest and cuts to public programs.

Lula also revamped his social media strategy, taking video selfies and even bought his first cellphone, while supporters carried out a feverish campaign to change the minds of family, friends and neighbors, and encourage them to vote after high levels of abstention.
His re-election marks another remarkable comeback for the man who grew up dirt poor in the northeast in a family of illiterate farmers.
Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months.
The charges, annulled on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.
In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but voters complain about the cost of living and a sense of insecurity.
Lula’s social policies became a point of tension as he expanded welfare programs during the campaign.
“Brazil needs more time with Lula, primarily because the country is on the verge of falling into the clutches of fascism,” Maria Fernanda Elisbao, a 21-year-old editorial assistant, told AFP.
A tricky term ahead
Lula heads into a fourth term with a country divided, with almost half of the nation voting against him and desperate for change.
“We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro.
Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030.
He will thus have spent 16 years in power, following his first stint as president from 2003 to 2010.
Lula is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right.
His options are also constrained by the economic outlook, with growth expected to slow.
He has also come under renewed pressure to confront rampant insecurity in a country plagued by criminal factions that sow terror in working-class neighbourhoods.
The president’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States.

Voters must “choose a country where the flag is respected,” he said, his raspy voice more hoarse than ever after a tireless campaign. He accused his rival of wanting to “govern with the American flag.” — AFP

4353787eaaeff6f0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will initiate disciplinary proceedings against Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) over actions deemed contrary to the coalition’s interests.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the decision was made at a PN Supreme Council meeting tonight, in accordance with Article 15 of the coalition’s constitution.

He said the article empowered the PN Supreme Council to take disciplinary action against any member party, individual member, affiliated party or associate member found to have acted against the coalition’s interests.

“The PN Supreme Council has the authority to take disciplinary action against any member party, individual member, affiliated party, or associate member by issuing a warning, suspending, or expelling the party or member concerned if they engage in conduct contrary to PN’s interests.
“PN will take the appropriate steps under the disciplinary proceedings and formally present the charges to the member party concerned, namely Bersatu,” he told a press conference after the meeting.
Takiyuddin said Bersatu would be given sufficient time to respond to the charges before any further action was taken.
Meanwhile, he said PN had decided to use its own logo in the 16th Melaka state election.
“The number of seats and candidates will be determined through a series of meetings to be held, during which these details will be finalised,” he said.
He said the court’s decision on Oct 22 to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) order suspending PN’s activities had enabled the coalition to resume its activities and functions as usual.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election. — Bernama

0baa6a6e0075d32c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — DAP chairman and Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today called for an open tender to develop a new local navigation application as an alternative to Waze, saying the government should replace what he described as the failed TuJu app.

In a statement, Lim said TuJu had become a “national embarrassment” and questioned why Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), the company behind the application, was awarded the project without an open tender.

“TuJu has failed miserably and Malaysians are asking why Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), the private company behind the TuJu navigation app, was given the approval without an open tender,” he said.

Lim said public scrutiny had extended to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, with questions raised over the app’s developer, ownership structure, links to former public officials, the absence of an open tender, and how the project was awarded.

“I have faith that there are many talented young Malaysians who can do a better job in designing a road navigation application better than TuJu, provided they are given the right opportunity, adequate funding and free competitive bidding,” he said.
Lim urged the government not to rush into recommending another navigation application until it had been proven, tested and shown to be reliable.
He also proposed that existing government funding be made available to local developers building minimum viable products (MVPs) without requiring them to give up equity.

Among the programmes cited were Cradle Fund’s CIP SPARK grant, which provides up to RM150,000 for early-stage innovation, and other funding initiatives offered by Cradle Fund and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), with support ranging from several hundred thousand ringgit to RM2 million for product development, commercialisation and business expansion.
Lim said competitive bidding, adequate funding and support for local talent would help produce a more effective homegrown navigation platform.
eef731b78e43ff2b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Malaysia has achieved its best-ever result at the World Barista Championship, with Tan Shing Win finishing second at the 2026 competition in Panama City, delivering a historic breakthrough for the country’s specialty coffee scene.

The reigning 2025 Malaysia Barista Champion secured his place on the podium after progressing through the preliminary rounds and semi-finals to reach the elite final six at the Panama Convention Center, where the competition ran from October 22 to 25.
Shing Win’s remarkable performance follows Malaysia’s previous best result at the prestigious global contest, when fellow Malaysian Jason Loo placed fourth at the 2025 World Barista Championship.

The achievement marks a defining moment for Malaysia’s coffee industry, demonstrating that the country’s baristas can compete with the world’s best on a stage traditionally dominated by established specialty coffee nations.

For Shing Win, who made his World Coffee Championships debut in Panama, the result is the culmination of nearly six years spent developing an understanding of coffee that extends well beyond the espresso machine.

Associated with One Half Roastery and Tri-Up Coffee, Shing Win has built his career across the specialty coffee supply chain, from sourcing green beans and working with producers to developing businesses and serving customers.

His journey into coffee began with a departure from conventional career expectations. Originally trained in finance and economics, he left office life after a short internship to pursue coffee full-time.
This was a decision that has now taken him to the podium of the world’s most prestigious barista competition.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Shing Win’s 2025 Malaysia Barista Championship routine. — Pictures from Instagram/World Barista Championship

At One Half Roastery in Petaling Jaya, he oversees business development and events, while his work with Tri-Up Coffee SEA involves green bean sourcing and market expansion. He has also served as store manager at artisanal bakery Dou Dou Bake.
That experience across the bean-to-cup journey informed a competition routine built around one of coffee’s most consequential variables: moisture.
During his 15-minute stage presentation, Shing Win explored how moisture levels influence coffee throughout its journey, from processing at origin and drying to the barista’s final extraction.
His central argument was that managing moisture is not simply a technical exercise, but a responsibility that helps preserve, develop and ultimately reveal a coffee’s flavour potential.
For the competition, he selected Hacienda La Esmeralda El Velo JH Natural Geisha, sourced through Tri-Up Coffee.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Shing Win (third from right) with other 2026 World Barista Championship finalists. — Picture from Instagram/World Barista Championship

The coffee underwent a complex processing method in which its husk was inoculated with bacteria and yeast derived from coffee material, followed by three days of anaerobic tank fermentation and a slow-drying phase under carefully controlled temperature and humidity conditions.
The selection reflected Shing Win’s wider approach to specialty coffee: understanding that what happens at origin is inseparable from what eventually reaches the consumer’s cup.

By connecting processing decisions with extraction and flavour, he presented the barista not merely as the final person in the chain, but as someone responsible for bringing the entire journey to its intended conclusion.
That philosophy has now carried him further than any Malaysian competitor before him at the World Barista Championship.

In a final featuring representatives from Australia, China, Canada, the United Arab Emirates and Thailand, Shing Win demonstrated that Malaysia’s coffee talent can hold its own among the international elite.
His podium finish also builds on the momentum generated by Loo’s fourth-place result last year, turning what was already a landmark performance into a new benchmark for Malaysian baristas.
For an industry that has spent years strengthening its roasting, sourcing, café and competition culture, Shing Win’s achievement is more than an individual accolade.
This shows how far Malaysia’s specialty coffee community has progressed and is a promising sign of what its next generation of competitors might achieve.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Alberto Escobon (left) of Storm Barista Attitude presenting Shing Win with his award. — YouTube screenshot/World Barista Championship
From leaving a conventional career to pursue coffee full-time to standing among the world’s top baristas, Shing Win’s journey has reached a historic high point in Panama.
Malaysia now has a new milestone to celebrate, and a new standard against which future World Barista Championship campaigns will be measured.

072add8fcbdb6a30: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is banking on its experience governing Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan as it seeks to win over voters in the Nov 14 Melaka election.
Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin said PH had experience managing the administrations in the three states and hoped Melaka voters would give the coalition the same opportunity.
He said PH believed its governing experience could serve as a foundation for leading Melaka.
"We know PH has a good track record, having successfully managed the administrations in Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan.

"If the people of Melaka give us the opportunity to lead the state, God willing, we will do our best, just as we have done in Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan," he said after the closing ceremony of Minggu Melaka Ceria in Tanjung Minyak last night.
Azman said PH's main aim was to give voters a choice in deciding which party should lead the state.
On Saturday, PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the coalition's 21 candidates for the Melaka polls, with PKR contesting nine seats, DAP seven and Amanah five.
The line-up comprises 13 new faces, five incumbent assemblymen retained as candidates and three candidates who had contested in previous elections.
Deputy Defence Minister and Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari is among the coalition's key candidates, while Azman will contest the Paya Rumput state seat.
f75bafcb86605431: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 26 — Two cars were badly damaged after being buried in a landslide near 33 Leisure Bay Condominium, Jalan Tanjung Tokong, Tanjung Bungah here yesterday.

Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations and Firefighting Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 6.50 pm before a team from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 7 pm.
“Upon arrival, we found that two cars, a BMW and a Honda City, had been buried by the landslide. Initial checks found that no one was involved in the incident.

“Rescue and monitoring operations are still underway, involving six personnel, including a supervisor and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), with assistance from the police at the scene,” he said in a statement tonight.
He said firefighting operations were still ongoing at the scene as of 7.45 pm, while the cause of the incident remained under investigation. — Bernama

179453d6e4d54b36: KUCHING, Oct 26 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was officially dissolved today, paving the way for the 13th Sarawak State Election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution on Friday (Oct 23) after receiving the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Article 21(4) of the State Constitution stipulates that the state election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution.
Attention now turns to the Election Commission (EC) to set a date for a special meeting to discuss key dates for the Sarawak polls.

EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said on Friday that the commission would determine the special meeting date after receiving formal notification of the dissolution from the Speaker of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly.

Meanwhile, Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said the state government would carry out its duties as a caretaker government during this period in accordance with all applicable constitutional requirements and conventions.
“Public administration and essential services will continue to ensure the needs and welfare of the people are safeguarded,” he said.
The current term of the 82-seat Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is due to expire in February 2027.
GPS won 76 of the 82 seats contested in the 12th Sarawak State Election on Dec 18, 2021, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) took four seats and DAP secured two.
The state’s political landscape changed after PSB dissolved in 2024, when three of its former state assemblymen joined the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a component party of GPS.
Another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, who represents Batu Lintang, subsequently left the party to sit as an Independent.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP. — Bernama
ef665b7ea191f5fa: LONDON: Storms battered northern Europe Sunday, killing a man, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes and disrupting travel and phone networks.
A man died when a tree fell on him in southwestern Scotland, while a runner in a marathon in northern France was injured when a tree was felled by strong winds during the race.

More than 82,000 homes in Britain, nearly 60,000 in France and at least 10,000 in Germany had power cuts inflicted by the passage of storms Boelo and Austen within 24 hours of each other, authorities in the countries said.

In the Argyll and Bute region of western Scotland, winds of up to 135km an hour were recorded. Trees and power cables brought down by the storm blocked roads and rail lines across Scotland and northern England.
Britain's Energy Networks Association said more than 400,000 homes had lost power at some stage during the storms.
Part of the pier at Brighton on the southern England coast, unused since a fire in 2003, blew away in Storm Austen on Friday.

The powerful winds also battered northern France across the Channel as Europe battled its first big autumn storms of the year. Experts have warned of more extreme weather events because of global warming.
Authorities warned of flood risk in regions in Scotland and England.
A runner was lightly injured in the northern French city of Lille near the start of the city's marathon, which was being staged for the first time in 31 years.
- WIDESPREAD POWER CUTS -
French energy company Enedis said that at the peak of storm Austen on Saturday, some 288,000 homes had no electricity.
Some 59,000 remained without power at midday Sunday, mainly in Normandy and Brittany. It said 2,600 Enedis technicians and contractors were working to re-establish power.

In Germany, Austen cut power to 10,000 homes in and around the southwestern town of Freiburg-Brisgau on Sunday. The town's main hospital said it had to limit service to emergency cases because of the blackout that also cut the mobile phone network.
Two people were seriously hurt Saturday by scaffolding blown away by storm Austen's winds during an autumn market at the town of Nastatten, German police said.
Germany's DWD weather agency predicted more powerful winds of up to 100kph on the northern coast on Sunday.
The storms also hit the Netherlands and Belgium, where falling trees injured four people in Brussels on Saturday.
Hundreds of flights were cancelled or diverted because of the storms across northern Europe.
Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, one of Europe's busiest hubs, cancelled dozens of flights Sunday.
AFP counted some 90 flights cancelled on the airport website, mainly to European cities including Paris, Rome and Dublin. Dozens of flights due to land at the airport were also cancelled.
Flights in northern England and Scotland were also hit by the storms.--AFP

91f50d0bb2ec0605: Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman will play off for the Bermuda Championship title on Monday after inclement weather forced officials to cancel the scheduled final round of the US PGA Tour event.
Organisers had tried to get Sunday's scheduled final round under way early but ended up cancelling play for the day as winds gusted up to 40 miles per hour and the weather deteriorated.
Hours after that decision was made, the tour announced that in view of the poor forecast for Monday officials had decided not to try to play a full round.

"Due to the unfavorable weather forecast for Monday at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship and the uncertainty surrounding the completion of the entire round on Monday, the tournament results will be considered final through 54 holes in accordance with PGA Tour regulations," the tour said in a statement.
"A playoff between Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman will be conducted to determine the champion," the statement said.
Smotherman carded a five-under par 66 on Saturday for a 16-under par total of 197.
He's trying to add his second title of the month after lifting his maiden PGA Tour trophy at the Utah Championship three weeks ago.
He was joined by Ireland's Power, whose four-under 67 on Saturday included a birdie at the wind-blown 17th that pulled him level with Smotherman atop the leaderboard.
The leading duo were two strokes clear of American Taylor Moore and Canadians Corey Conners and Ben Silverman, who all finished 54 holes at 14-under par. — AFP
f11a6075783a6136: KUCHING: The Sarawak assembly was officially dissolved today, paving the way for the 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution on Friday after receiving the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Article 21(4) of the State Constitution stipulates that the state election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution.
Attention now turns to the Election Commission (EC) to set a date for a special meeting to determine key dates for the polls.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said on Oct 23 that the commission would set the meeting date after receiving formal notification of the dissolution from the Speaker.

Meanwhile, Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said the state government would continue operating as a caretaker government in accordance with constitutional requirements and conventions.
"Public administration and essential services will continue to ensure the needs and welfare of the people are safeguarded," he said.
The current term of the 82-seat assembly was due to expire in February 2027.
GPS won 76 of the 82 seats contested in the 12th Sarawak state election on Dec 18, 2021, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats and DAP secured two.
Sarawak's political landscape changed after PSB was dissolved in 2024, with three of its former assemblymen joining Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a component party of GPS.
Another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, who represents Batu Lintang, subsequently left the party and became an Independent.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.
507d58ba48bdf806: RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Authority said Sunday that nearly 2,700 people had been displaced by an Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron launched after two soldiers were killed in an attack nearby.

Following Friday's attack, Israeli forces entered the Hebron neighbourhood of Ein Deir Baha, where the assailants lived, and ordered residents to pack up and leave after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged a major operation in the occupied territory.

"More than 2,670 Palestinians have been forcibly displaced from their homes in Hebron by Israeli occupation forces, the majority of them women, children, and elderly people, according to data from Hebron Municipality," the Palestinian prime minister's office said on X.

A convoy of Israeli military and police vehicles accompanied by soldiers was seen in Hebron on Sunday, making its way down a street blocked to civilian traffic by parked cars and motorbikes, AFP images showed.
Local shopkeeper Higazi al-Tamimi, who also plays a leadership role in the evacuated neighbourhood, accused Israeli soldiers of beating him as he attempted to go to his home.
"I remember one or two people starting to strike my legs, chest and shoulders. One of them even hit me on the head," he said from a hospital bed, with his leg thickly bandaged.
"They then pushed me backwards, and I kept moving until I reached a safe area."--AFP

This also includes strategies to increase the value of local products, reduce reliance on raw material exports and expand industrial opportunities and income for smallholders.

Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu) will ask the economy minister about the government's assessment of the challenges facing the middle-income group, including rising housing, education, healthcare and family-related expenses, despite some households not qualifying for assistance.

f1dd789f36cb644d: BEIJING: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.
US crude futures were down US$1.60, or 1.55 per cent, at US$101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures were down US$1.56 or 1.34 per cent at US$115.16.

Prices had settled nearly US$3 higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up six per cent and West Texas Immediate ended 2.3 per cent higher.
Attacks continued over the weekend with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones.
The top oil exporter restarted partial operations at its main airport on Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks even as the militant group vowed to keep targeting the facility.
4f61aa0cd3f76a90: TANAH MERAH: Two men, including a Pakistani, were arrested after nearly 20,000 sticks of smuggled cigarettes were seized in two separate raids yesterday.
The raids were conducted by the General Operations Force (GOF) 9th Battalion at Kampung Bukit Nangka and Kampung Paralla Dua between 4pm and 5pm following intelligence gathering.
Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the first raid was conducted at a house in Kampung Bukit Nangka, Gual Ipoh, at 4pm.
He said officers arrested a 33-year-old local man after finding 6,080 sticks of smuggled cigarettes worth RM11,456 in a sack placed near a pile of wood in front of the house.
"The suspect claimed he obtained the cigarettes from an individual known as 'Chong' and intended to sell them around Tanah Merah," he said in a statement.
Radzi said the second raid was conducted at a shop-house in Kampung Paralla Dua at 5pm.
"An inspection of the premises uncovered a sack containing several cartons of smuggled cigarettes, totalling 13,880 sticks and worth more than RM26,000.

"We arrested a 55-year-old Pakistani man for further investigation. During questioning, he claimed the cigarettes had been supplied by two people who delivered them to the premises for sale and distribution," he said.
Both suspects were arrested under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act.
Radzi said the suspects had been handed over to the Tanah Merah district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department for further investigation.
"The GOF will continue monitoring the border to prevent incursions and smuggling," he said.
2844c4fe1c312b60: ROTTERDAM, (Netherlands):

American teenagers Claire Pease and Reese Esponda reaped the reward of high-difficulty routines to take the top two places in the women's floor excercise Sunday on the final day of the World Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam.
Their medals allowed the United States, who collected eight medals, three of them gold, to edge China for the top spot in the medal count.
China finished with seven medals including three golds, the last of them earlier Sunday when Zou Jingyuan continued his domination of the men's parallel bars.

In the women's floor event, the 17-year-old Pease scored 13.866. Esponda, also 17, was second 13.566, 0.010 off French 16-year-old Maiana Prat and Britain's Abigail Martin, the oldest of the quartet at 18, on a tiebreak.
Prat, who had the lowest degree of difficulty, was awarded bronze because her execution score was better than Martin's.
The American women put on a spectacular show in Rotterdam, led by Skye Blakely, who won gold in the all-around and bronze on the uneven bars and vault.
The Texan, a model of resilience, was the feel-good story of this week in the Netherlands.
She was forced to withdraw from the 2020 Olympic Games, held in 2021 in Tokyo, and the 2024 Paris Games, with injuries.
Zou was again untouchable on the bars.
The 28-year-old finished on 15.733 for his fifth world title in the event.

Illia Kovtun, who left his native Ukraine after the Russian invasion and represents Croatia, was a distant second on 14.900, just ahead of Russian Daniel Marinov, representing World Gymnastics, on 14.866.
On the beam, Algeria's Kaylia Nemour claimed her second gold in two days as she edged China's Zhang Qingying a tiebreak.
Brazil's Flavia Saraiva was third.
The 19-year-old Nemour finished tied with Zhang on 14.566 points.
Nemour rebounded with two golds after finishing fourth in Friday's all-around after errors on the vault and the uneven Bars.
After finishing close to tears on Friday, Nemour beamed as she received a standing ovation on Sunday.
She said she was happy "even if it doesn't make up for the all-around competition."
Armenian Artur Davtyan opened the day's competition by winning the men's vault.
The 34-year-old colected 14.850 points to finish ahead of Britain's Jake Jarman on 14.650 with Norway's Sebastian Sponevik third.

A double Olympic medalist in the event - with a bronze in Tokyo in 2020 and a silver in Paris in 2024 — the veteran from Yerevan claimed his second vault world title, following victory in Liverpool in 2022.
Taiwan's Chia-Hung Tang brought the competition to a close by winning the horizontal bar ahead of Japan's Shinnosuke Oka and Russian Sergei Naidin.
At age 30, Tang claimed his first world title on the apparatus that had earned him an Olympic bronze in Paris. — AFP

f37ebaa413d70a3f: AUSTIN: Kimi Antonelli has given his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff nine wins to get excited about this season but the Italian's dominant drive from pole position at Sunday's US Grand Prix took that to another level.
The 20-year-old, set to become the youngest ever Formula One champion in Mexico next weekend, won by more than 13 seconds on a one-stop strategy.
His teammate and closest title rival George Russell, now 123 points behind with 125 still to be won, started sixth and finished eighth - just enough to keep the championship hanging by a thread.
"On Kimi's side the main headline is that for me (that's) the best race that he's delivered so far," Wolff said.
"Getting off the start with the inferior tyre and then controlling it (the race) at all times. The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional.
"I think he's outperformed the car. His driving style just glues with the car."

Wolff, reminded that Antonelli has had some special wins already this season including at his home Italian Grand Prix from the back of the grid as well as Monaco and Spa, accepted that sometimes he struggled to remember past races.
"Both of them were pretty good," he said in reference to Monza. "But the headline, this is the best, we can keep."
Antonelli was happy to agree with the boss.

"I think it was one of the best, because of how we built up during the weekend," he told reporters. "And, you know, it was a great team effort as well today, especially with the strategy, believing in the one-stop. And, yeah, it was a really great team effort, and they all deserve this result today.
"Monza, we clearly had the fastest car. We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back," he added.

"But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick. But definitely, Monza was a super special one, and one that I will remember forever. But, you know, this one probably, in terms of execution, was better ... the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good."

71a8c07aab28c7fd: RIYADH: US Central Command on Sunday said it helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via the Strait of Hormuz since summer, bypassing an Iranian blockade.
"U.S. forces reach the milestone of assisting Gulf partners in exporting more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer," CENTCOM said in a statement posted on X.

"More than 3,000 commercial vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz with support from CENTCOM forces over the last six months," it added, stating that "over 95% of ships navigating the Strait of Hormuz have sailed through safely."

"Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people," said CENTCOM chief admiral Brad Cooper, who was visiting US troops in Hormuz.
Iran has seized control over the vital waterway since the Middle East war erupted with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic on Feb 28.
It has demanded permission for ships to transit the strait, through which a fifth of global oil exports normally pass.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this month that Iran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that Teheran's economy was "in total and complete freefall."
"The Straits of Hormuz are open. There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So they've lost complete control of the Straits," he said.
According to data from the maritime tracking firm Kpler, crude oil exports reached pre-war levels in September, with at least 16.5 million barrels leaving the region excluding Iran.--AFP
7232fd1bfd9349fe: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has completed 41 of the 60 sub-strategies under the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (NACS) 2024-2028, marking progress in efforts to strengthen governance and combat corruption.

Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Senior Director Datuk Idris Zaharudin said the achievement reflected the government's efforts to translate policy commitments into concrete action across ministries and agencies.

Launched in May 2024 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, NACS provides a comprehensive framework to strengthen governance, integrity and accountability through legislative reforms, institutional improvement, the integration of anti-corruption education into school and university curricula, and stronger private sector accountability through corporate integrity programmes.

Speaking to the New Straits Times, Idris said the strategy was not merely a continuation of the previous anti-corruption plan, but an adoption of a more structured, phased and measurable approach to implementation.

"NACS was developed as a comprehensive strategic framework integrating legislative reforms, system enhancements, educational empowerment and collective involvement from the private sector and civil society," he said.
Among its key achievements are the enactment of the Border Control and Protection Agency Act 2025, the Government Procurement Act 2025 and the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.

NACS has also driven amendments to the Immigration Act 2025 and the Whistleblower Protection Act 2025, alongside the implementation of job rotation policies and the Demerit Performance Evaluation (DEEP) system.

Other measures include guidelines clarifying the roles and responsibilities of National Audit Department officers stationed in internal audit units at ministries, government departments, agencies and state secretariats.
Idris said NACS should not be treated as a static policy document, as governance challenges and institutional reforms need to evolve.
"More importantly, NACS is not viewed as a static policy document. It is a living document that evolves alongside current challenges and dynamic institutional reform needs," he said.
He said a key focus was ensuring that progress could be monitored systematically through two digital dashboards developed by the division and hosted on MACC servers.

"The r-NACS dashboard serves as an internal quarterly performance-monitoring tool between the NACS Secretariat and lead agencies, while the d-NACS dashboard provides public access to implementation information, including completed sub-strategies and key outputs by agency," he said.
Idris said the data-driven approach would strengthen accountability among implementing agencies besides allowing problems to be identified and addressed more quickly.
He added that the main challenge was ensuring reforms were implemented effectively at operational and grassroots levels.
"The primary challenge now lies not at the strategy formulation stage, but in the capability to execute it effectively and comprehensively at the grassroots level," he said.
The reforms extend beyond enforcement, with education identified as a core component in building a long-term culture of integrity.
Integrity and anti-corruption modules have been incorporated into higher-learning institutions, alongside efforts to strengthen integrity-related content in primary and secondary school curricula.
Idris described education as a long-term investment in developing a generation capable of strengthening the country's institutions and leadership.
"Education is no longer considered a supporting component, but a core strategy in building a sustainable anti-corruption ecosystem," he said.
The strategy also emphasises the role of the private sector, particularly in government procurement, where public and corporate interests intersect.

Companies participating in public procurement are required to declare their beneficiary owners, while those bidding for government construction contracts worth more than RM100 million are subject to measures promoting the MS ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management Systems (ABMS) certification.

Tax incentives for companies obtaining ISO 37001 ABMS accreditation are also among measures aimed at encouraging stronger corporate anti-corruption practices, complementing corporate liability provisions under Section 17A of the MACC Act 2009.
Meanwhile, Malaysia aims to rank among the top 25 countries in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) by 2030.

A special CPI task force has been established to identify gaps and formulate strategic interventions in enforcement, public fund management, business competitiveness, investment risks and legislative reform.
Idris said the anti-corruption agenda required sustained participation across the public sector, corporate world and civil society.

"The true effectiveness of NACS will not only be measured by the number of sub-strategies completed, but by the extent to which systemic change can be felt by the public through services that are more transparent, efficient and fair," he said.
With 41 sub-strategies completed, the next phase will focus on sustaining implementation, strengthening coordination and ensuring reforms translate into lasting institutional change.
NACS succeeds the National Anti-Corruption Plan (NACP) 2019-2023 and aims to position Malaysia as a corrupt-free and prosperous nation.
It comprises 60 sub-strategies overseen by 20 government ministries, departments and agencies, including MACC and the National Audit Department.

0ca6fb10d8c1e1d3: KUALA LUMPUR: Southeast Asian countries, including Malaysia, have announced hundreds of billions of dollars in green investments.
The real test is turning these commitments into projects on the ground.
For Malaysia, closing the gap between ambition and execution is crucial to boosting industrial competitiveness and attracting investment.
Delays, infrastructure bottlenecks and financing constraints risk slowing the energy transition.

Maybank group chief sustainability officer Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin said the biggest hurdle was no longer a shortage of capital or climate commitments, but a lack of bankable projects capable of delivering measurable emissions reductions
"The money has always been there but what remains scarce is the number of bankable projects available," he told Business Times.
The gap between climate ambitions and actual investment is evident globally.

CDP's "From Plans to Capital" report found that 72 per cent of nearly 12,000 companies reporting through the platform had initiatives to reduce emissions, but only 11 per cent disclosed capital expenditure aligned with their transition strategies

About US$540 billion in green capital expenditure has been announced across Southeast Asia's power and electric vehicle value chains through 2030. However, only around US$315 billion is on a credible path to deployment, Shahril said.
The problem extends beyond financing.
Regulatory uncertainty, permitting delays, grid connection constraints and unclear power purchase agreements have undermined project viability despite investor interest.
Bain's 2026 report on Southeast Asia's green economy found that 50 to 60 per cent of renewable energy projects in Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia were cancelled between 2021 and 2025, Shahril said.
The findings highlight barriers beyond the availability of capital.

The challenge is particularly pressing as Malaysia pursues its National Energy Transition Roadmap, which aims for renewable energy to account for 35 per cent of installed electricity-generation capacity by 2030 and 70 per cent by 2050.
For Shahril, the priority is to ensure that businesses, financiers and policymakers can translate those targets into viable projects, the infrastructure needed to support them and measurable results.
FROM AMBITION TO BANKABILITY
A credible transition plan must go beyond a company's pledge to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.
It needs to establish a baseline for current emissions, set interim reduction targets, identify the required investments and demonstrate how they will be funded.
He said banks and investors needed to know whether a company's targets were achievable and adequately funded.

Shahril identified five essential elements: a reliable emissions baseline; a defined pathway with interim milestones; a capital expenditure plan linked to expected returns; alignment with recognised sustainability standards; and strong governance, accountability and regular reporting.
The Joint Committee on Climate Change has agreed to adopt the Asean Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance as the basis for Malaysia's taxonomy, Shahril said.
Independent assessments can further strengthen investor confidence by validating a project's environmental credentials and giving lenders a clearer basis for evaluating its risks.

Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, for instance, acted as sustainability framework adviser in developing Tenaga Nasional Bhd's Transition Finance Framework. The framework received a second-party opinion from Morningstar Sustainalytics and referenced the Asean Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance Version 2 and the Asean Transition Finance Guidance
Malakoff Corporation Bhd's Sustainable Finance Framework also received a 'Gold' Impact Assessment and a second-party opinion from MARC Ratings Bhd.
Such assessments translate broad climate ambitions into defined criteria that investors and credit committees can evaluate.
Shahril said the assessments also help distinguish companies backing their climate targets with actual investment from those making long-term pledges without corresponding near-term spending.
FINANCING THE TRANSITION, NOT JUST GREEN PROJECTS
A further challenge is decarbonising industries that cannot immediately abandon conventional energy sources.

Financing only businesses that are already green would leave some of the most difficult emissions reductions unaddressed, particularly in emerging economies where industrial activity and energy security remain critical.

Companies unable to switch technologies overnight need credible transition plans. These should demonstrate measurable improvements in emissions intensity, avoid locking in high-carbon assets indefinitely and allow for deeper decarbonisation as technology and infrastructure mature.
Shahril said two financing transactions illustrate how this can work.

Malakoff's RM450 million SRI Sukuk Murabahah financed solar and hydropower projects, as well as identify the eligible project, which was assessed against the Asean Taxonomy's Amber Tier 2 lifecycle emissions thresholds.
The classification recognises a transitional role for high-efficiency gas while taking account of emissions criteria and energy security.
In Singapore, Maybank, DBS and OCBC jointly extended a S$500 million transition loan to YTL PowerSeraya.
The financing supports a 600-megawatt hydrogen-ready combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power plant.
Shahril said it was the first transition finance deal aligned with the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy.
The H-class turbine is estimated to cut carbon dioxide emissions intensity by about 10 per cent compared with older F-class technology.
It can co-fire up to 50 per cent hydrogen at launch and could eventually be retrofitted to run fully on hydrogen as supply develops.
The project is targeted for completion by the end of 2027.
When commercially viable hydrogen supplies become available, co-firing 30 per cent hydrogen could reduce emissions intensity by a further 12 per cent, he said.
These targets give investors measurable benchmarks for assessing environmental performance and progress against the project's transition pathway.
However, lenders must also account for risks such as delays in hydrogen supply and supporting infrastructure.
Transition finance therefore requires the same rigour as conventional lending, with clear eligibility criteria, quantifiable performance indicators and contingency plans.
The quality of transition data is also increasingly influencing capital allocation.
Indeed, CDP's Corporate Health Check 2026 reported that financial institutions managing US$145 trillion in assets use transition-plan data in their due diligence.
Companies achieving CDP's leadership level also identified a combined US$218 billion in environmental opportunities.
The message for businesses is that credible data and measurable outcomes are becoming central to attracting capital, rather than optional additions to sustainability disclosures.
THE RISING COST OF NOT TRANSITIONING
For companies concerned about the upfront costs of decarbonisation, the economic risks of inaction are becoming harder to ignore.
The International Energy Agency estimates that Southeast Asia's fossil fuel import bill could rise from just over US$80 billion in 2024 to around US$245 billion by 2035 without structural changes.
Delivering on announced pledges could reduce that projected bill by roughly half, Shahril said.
The region's reliance on imported fuels exposes businesses and economies to price volatility, geopolitical disruption and higher energy costs.
Coal accounts for about half of Southeast Asia's electricity generation.
Shahril said regional coal demand had grown by about eight per cent annually. Coal's share of the energy mix rose from 20 per cent in 2015 to 30 per cent in 2026.
For Malaysia, the energy transition is also becoming a factor in attracting investment in data centres, advanced manufacturing and other electricity-intensive industries.
Peak electricity demand is projected to rise from 21.3 gigawatts in 2026 to 33.5 gigawatts by 2035, according to the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry.
Data centres could account for about a third of electricity consumption by 2035, compared with around seven per cent today, Shahril said.
Meanwhile, 90 per cent of data centre operators surveyed in Asean identified grid-connection delays as a major constraint, with many willing to pay a premium for a guaranteed connection date.
"These companies are then choosing locations based on how quickly they can get reliable, increasingly green power.
"For Malaysia, the energy transition is therefore an economic policy. It can shape where companies invest and how industries compete."
MAKING THE TRANSITION COMMERCIALLY VIABLE
Businesses do not necessarily need to begin with their most expensive decarbonisation investments.
A phased approach can prioritise projects with relatively quick payback periods, including energy-efficiency improvements, rooftop solar and battery storage to reduce peak-demand charges.
The Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme also provides companies with a route to secure renewable electricity without developing generation assets themselves.
Matching long-term investments with appropriately structured financing can help spread upfront costs and improve project economics.
Technology selection is equally important, Shahril said, as not every emerging solution will deliver the expected commercial or environmental returns.
Companies must assess technology maturity, cost, performance and scalability before committing capital.
Malaysia's own programmes also demonstrate how transition investment can generate domestic economic benefits.
The 2026 Feed-in Tariff round is expected to catalyse RM4.3 billion in investment, create 7,738 jobs and generate about RM617 million in demand for locally manufactured equipment, he said.

These benefits strengthen the case for treating the energy transition as an industrial development strategy that can support local supply chains and employment, rather than solely as an environmental obligation.
BRING BANKS IN BEFORE PROJECTS ARE DESIGNED
Earlier engagement between businesses and financial institutions is another important factor in turning projects into bankable investments.
"It is incredibly critical, yet still underused. In fact, it is one of the biggest factors in whether a plan can reach financing at all," Shahril said.
When banks are approached only after a project has been designed, its financing structure may not adequately address technical assumptions, environmental requirements or risks.
Engaging lenders earlier allows companies to incorporate taxonomy criteria, disclosure requirements and investor expectations before key decisions are finalised.

Tenaga Nasional's Transition Finance Framework, developed with Maybank Investment Banking Group, enables the utility to issue green, sustainability and transition-labelled instruments, including SRI sukuk.
The framework comes as TNB plans to invest RM43 billion in strengthening the grid between 2025 and 2027, supporting the infrastructure needed to accommodate Malaysia's changing energy mix.
Shahril said YTL PowerSeraya engaged its financing banks early and throughout the process.
This allowed the CCGT's technical design, emissions performance and taxonomy alignment to be considered in the credit assessment from the outset.
The JC3 Climate Finance Innovation Lab reflects a similar approach.
a60de866005804ab: KUALA LUMPUR: Vista's flight traffic in Malaysia rose 18 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, higher than the 14 per cent growth recorded across Asia Pacific.
Vista chief business officer Youssef Mouallem said the growth is supported by industrial activity in Malaysia and demand from business travellers seeking greater flexibility and shorter travel time.

"We see a big part of the industrial attraction in Malaysia. Business aviation has always been a tool for enabling business and we're seeing it come into play with that," he told Business Times in an exclusive interview recently.
Mouallem said private aviation demand in Malaysia is growing faster than the wider Asia Pacific market and he expects the trend to continue in the second half of the year.

"Malaysia is growing ahead of the region. That's year-on-year. We've seen an accelerating trend. So, expect this to continue and probably even accelerate further in the second half (of the year)," he added.

Vista is a global business aviation group operating VistaJet, which provides private jet services through its fleet and membership programmes, and XO, which offers on-demand access to about 2,000 vetted aircraft worldwide.
Malaysia is Vistajet's first market in Southeast Asia, having entered into the country in 2008 before expanding across the region.
Mouallem said that Southeast Asia remains an important market for Vista and serves as a link to Oceania.
"The growth rates are higher than our global average, so it's a growth market for us, and we continue to invest in that," he added.
Mouallem said XO provides access to a global marketplace of about 2,000 vetted aircraft, allowing customers to check aircraft availability and pricing before booking.
Elsewhere in Southeast Asia, Vista also recorded strong traffic growth in several markets in the first half of 2026.
Singapore's flight traffic rose 58 per cent year-on-year, while flight hours increased 51 per cent.
Indonesia recorded 27 per cent growth, while Vietnam and the Philippines posted an increase of 64 per cent and 62 per cent, respectively.
Mouallem said Vista is also seeing younger customers entering private aviation, particularly in Asia.
About 47 per cent of Vista's new flyers in 2025 are below 45 years old.

"These are entrepreneurs. These are tech millionaires. These are AI and crypto players. There's a lot of that wealth coming into the industry," Mouallem said, adding that these customers are looking for flexibility, quicker access to aircraft and the ability to book closer to their travel date.
Vista's average booking lead time has fallen from about 14 days to nine days, he said.
"They want the flexibility. They don't want to commit early and they want the access," he added.
Another trend that Vista is seeing in Southeast Asia is the demand for regional and long-range business jets.
Mouallem said the Bombardier Challenger 600 aircraft remains in demand for regional flying, while longer-haul demand includes the large-cabin Bombardier Global 6000 and the Global 7500 aircraft.
Vista is also upgrading its Global 7500 fleet to Global 8000.
"We've completed 11 out of our fleet of 18, and the other seven will be done before the end of the year," Mouallem said.
On fuel costs, he said higher jet fuel prices have not had a significant impact on Vista's flying demand.
"I wouldn't say it's a concern. It's a dynamic that you have to deal with. We haven't seen a real impact on the flying trend or on demand," he added.
Mouallem also said further growth in Asia's private aviation market depends on improvements across the wider business aviation ecosystem, including service levels, governance and digitalisation.

"For the overall industry to thrive, you need the whole ecosystem to move forward. We'd expect all of the other players to really improve service levels, safety, and governance. There's a lot of grey market or parallel brokering, so that's something that does not necessarily help the industry."

"It allows access but it does not allow the industry to develop as a whole," he said, adding that greater digitalisation is needed across services such as flight planning, fixed-base operators (FBOs), onboard servicing and catering to provide a more integrated experience for customers.

4ce53ef0c476a18d: PETALING JAYA: While having a will can spare a family a great deal of uncertainty, simply signing one does not guarantee everything will unfold smoothly.

A useful will needs to reflect not only who should inherit but also how those assets are likely to be managed, transferred and used. When circumstances change or important roles are left unclear, a document intended to simplify matters can instead create complications.
Here are four common mistakes you should avoid.
1. Dividing property without thinking through the consequences
Leaving one property to several beneficiaries may appear equitable, but shared ownership can become complicated - even fractious - once different expectations come into play.

One beneficiary may want to sell while another prefers to keep the property, creating disagreements over use, maintenance, rental income or eventual disposal. Matters become even more difficult if minors are involved, since children cannot independently manage or sell property.

A practical estate plan considers how the asset is likely to function after death - whether it should be sold and the proceeds divided, transferred to one beneficiary, or managed through another arrangement rather than simply split among several names.
2. Forgetting the people who make the will work
Beneficiaries are only one part of the estate-planning process: a will also depends on the people entrusted to carry out its instructions and protect the interests of those involved.

An executor administers the estate, settles debts and taxes, and oversees the distribution of assets according to the will. A guardian may be needed to care for minor children, while a trustee can hold and manage assets until beneficiaries are old enough or until agreed conditions are met.
Failing to appoint suitable people can leave a family facing delays, disputes or uncertainty at an already difficult time.

Just as importantly, those chosen should be willing, capable and sufficiently organised to take on the responsibility. Naming someone simply because they are close to you does not necessarily make them the right person for the role.
3. Writing a will once and never looking at it again

A will should not be treated as a document that can be signed once and forgotten indefinitely. Marriage, divorce, the birth of a child, the purchase of a major asset, relocation overseas, or the death of a beneficiary, executor or trustee can all alter what makes sense for a family.
Reviewing a will every few years - and after major changes in personal or financial circumstances - helps ensure its instructions still reflect the life you are actually living.
That review does not necessarily require a complete rewrite. Sometimes the more important question is whether the people, assets and arrangements named years earlier still make sense today.
4. Choosing beneficiaries without planning for what happens next
Estate planning is not only about deciding who receives an asset; it is also about considering whether that person is in a position to manage it responsibly.

A young beneficiary may not yet be ready to handle a large sum of money, while a minor cannot independently deal with many legal or financial matters. In such situations, a trustee or guardian may be needed to manage the inheritance until the beneficiary reaches a suitable age or meets agreed conditions.

It is also worth thinking beyond the most obvious scenario. If a sole beneficiary dies before the person making the will, for instance, the estate may become harder to distribute unless an alternative beneficiary or arrangement has been provided for.

The broader lesson is that a will should do more than divide possessions: it should anticipate how assets will move from one generation to the next, who will oversee that process, whether the people receiving them are equipped to manage what has been left behind.

Ultimately, a clear will cannot eliminate every disagreement or complication, but thoughtful planning can greatly reduce the risk of leaving loved ones with a legal and financial puzzle at the very moment they are least prepared to deal with one.

f0ec4cd2fbceb27e: What if I told you that the most important meeting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim had in China last month wasn't with officials of Alibaba, Huawei or Geely, but with a company that didn't exist four years ago?

In Hangzhou, Agibot, a Shanghai humanoid robot maker founded only in 2023, pledged a potential RM1 billion investment in Malaysia by 2035 along with 5,000 jobs, according to The Edge. Sure, a potential pledge is not money in the bank, but the company making it is no minnow.

Agibot shipped more humanoids than any other firm last year - 5,168 of them according to research firm Omdia; and International Data Corporation (IDC), an American market intelligence firm, has it on top again so far this year. To boot, it rolled its 20,000th robot off the line in September. A company not yet old enough for kindergarten is out-building every rival.

I've spent years in the robotics industry, between Silicon Valley, Shenzhen and Singapore, and if there's one thing I've learnt, it's that the products which end up defining an era almost always start out clumsy, expensive and easy to laugh at, right up until they aren't.

The personal computer, the internet, the laptop, the smartphone and now artificial intelligence (AI) all followed that script. Case in point: in 2007, Microsoft's then chief executive Steve Ballmer told USA Today that "there's no chance that the iPhone is going to get any significant market share. No chance." Within a decade, Apple had become America's biggest smartphone brand.

Today it's driverless cars, with Alphabet's Waymo giving more than 500,000 paid rides a week across more than a dozen American cities, and next, I would wager, comes the humanoid robot, the defining product of the next five to 10 years.
From stumbling to sprinting
If that sounds far-fetched, consider that in April last year, the winner of the world's first robot half marathon in Beijing limped home in two hours and 40 minutes.

This April, a robot built by Chinese phone maker Honor completed the same race on its own, more than six minutes faster than the men's world record. That's right, in a single year robots went from stumbling to beating the best time any human has ever run. Let that sink in for a bit.
And this is no lone show pony. IDC estimates that nearly 25,000 humanoids were shipped in the first half of this year, up a whopping 432%, with Chinese makers building more than 95% of them.

Here's the kicker: they're getting cheaper at a mind-blowing pace. Unitree's G1 launched in 2024 at 99,000 yuan (RM60,500), yet just over a year later its smaller R1 arrived at 39,900 yuan (RM24,400), less than half the price.

The Americans aren't sitting still either, with Tesla saying it is converting part of its Fremont, California, car plant to make its Optimus robot, which Elon Musk calls "probably the biggest product ever".
So how big could this get? IDC expects annual shipments to pass 750,000 by 2030, and Morgan Stanley reckons more than a billion could be in use by 2050.
Not quite ready for your living room

Mind you, none of these machines is ready to babysit your children, and electric vehicle news site Electrek reported that it could find no evidence Tesla built even hundreds of the 5,000 to 10,000 Optimus robots Musk had talked of making last year.

Even Agibot's founder, Deng Taihua, has said that robots in the home face different challenges from those in factories, since they have to weave between furniture and everyday clutter. That's precisely why factories and warehouses will come first, then hospitals and hotels, and only then the gloriously messy Malaysian home, shoes piled at the front door and all.
Why Malaysia should grab this with both hands

Six years ago, I wrote that jobs demanding dexterity in unpredictable surroundings were among the most resilient to automation for the next 20 years. With robots now loading car parts on a BMW line, I can't help but feel I was far too generous with my timeline.

But here's the thing: for Malaysia, that is mostly good news. We relied on about 2.1 million documented foreign workers as of October 2025 and the government has capped their share of the workforce at 13% and wants it down to 10% by 2030. Meanwhile, economy minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir told Parliament this month that we will become an aged nation, with 14% of the population aged 65 and above, by 2048.

We're short of hands and greying fast, and a machine that can lift, sort and fetch around the clock eases both problems. Agibot is already on the ground here, running an experience centre with developer I-Berhad at i-City in Shah Alam.

So what should Putrajaya do now? Get that "potential" RM1 billion signed, sealed and delivered. After Budget 2027, Treasury secretary-general Johan Mahmood Merican said the government was open to using foreign worker levies to "finance mechanisation", and that money could help pay for the first humanoids on Malaysian factory floors, on condition that some of them were assembled here.

Agibot did not exist four years ago, and today it wants to spend RM1 billion in Malaysia. Give its robots five to ten more years and the question on our factory floors won't be whether to hire one, but how soon we can do it.
The writer can be contacted at kathirgugan@protonmail.com. The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
7c92f6d39a40d61f: SYDNEY: Australia's prime minister and fellow parliamentarians led sombre tributes Monday to "beacon of decency" and colleague Helen Haines, who remains in hospital after being struck by a car outside her office a week ago.

A widely liked independent lawmaker known for campaigning against corruption and for action on climate change, the alleged attack on Haines has prompted soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare.

Prime minister Anthony Albanese pointed to her empty seat while paying tribute to the lawmaker's "empathy, kindness and compassion" as Australia's parliament met for the first time since the incident.
"The shock from what happened last Monday is like a stone in our hearts," Albanese said.
"Right now, our friend and colleague is in hospital, grievously injured. The shape of her life and her family's lives changed forever," he said.
He paid tribute to the bystanders who offered help to Haines, describing it as "the best of the Australian character".
And he bemoaned a rise in public anger "that distorts and corrodes our public discourse".
"We are seeing a normalisation of the language of grievance and violence," Albanese said.
Deputy prime minister Richard Marles described her as a "beacon of decency".
Haines remains in a serious but stable condition in a Melbourne hospital as of Monday morning.
Her husband, Phil, has said that surgeons had been forced to amputate both her legs in an effort to save her.
Haines's alleged attacker - 43-year-old Brendan Nugent - fronted court for the first time on Wednesday.

He has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
His motive remains unknown and authorities will not speculate while the investigation is ongoing.
But police said last week they were examining all possible leads, including that Nugent may have held radical anti-government views.
They have documented a surge in threats against Australian lawmakers in recent years - with 1,067 incidents reported to police in 2025 alone.
Federal police chief Krissy Barrett said on Sunday there was a correlation between intense political rhetoric and threats against lawmakers.
"Sometimes it's very immediate," she told national broadcaster ABC.
"Words matter, and we do see the flow on impact from that."
a3469be99339319e: BRUSSELS: Pihak berkuasa Perancis menahan 1,314 individu semasa tunjuk perasaan di seluruh negara pada Sabtu lalu, manakala 53 anggota keselamatan cedera, lapor Agensi Anadolu memetik Kementerian Dalam Negeri Perancis pada Ahad.

Menurut kementerian itu, seramai 410,000 orang menyertai tunjuk perasaan pada Sabtu di seluruh Perancis, termasuk 110,000 di Paris.
Bagaimanapun, kesatuan sekerja menganggarkan kehadiran di seluruh negara mencecah hampir 800,000 orang, dengan 250,000 penunjuk perasaan berada di ibu negara.
Kementerian memaklumkan 24 premis perniagaan dirompak semasa tunjuk perasaan itu berbanding 1,522 premis seminggu sebelumnya, menunjukkan penurunan lebih 98%.

Menurutnya, keadaan jauh lebih tenang berbanding tunjuk perasaan pada 17 Okt lalu, apabila beberapa premis perniagaan dirompak di bandar raya berkenaan.
Di Paris, 142 individu ditahan, termasuk 126 yang direman, menurut polis.
Dua premis perniagaan mengalami kerosakan, dengan satu daripadanya turut dirompak, manakala polis menghalang penunjuk perasaan memasuki sebuah lagi premis.
Sementara itu, seorang individu mengalami kecederaan parah pada tangan semasa tunjuk perasaan di Clermont-Ferrand, walaupun pihak berkuasa mengesahkan tiada kecacatan atau kehilangan jari.
Seorang lagi individu cedera parah di tangan semasa tunjuk perasaan di Toulouse.
260cb35659e14b57: KUALA LUMPUR: Ta Ann Holdings Bhd has emerged as the most attractive plantation stock in terms of potential share-price gains, with a target price of RM8.55 implying a 50.5 per cent upside, as improving production, earnings prospects and dividend yields underpin investment interest in the sector.

Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) has named Ta Ann, Genting Plantations Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and Sarawak Plantation Bhd as "Outperform" picks, while maintaining "Neutral" calls on IOI Corp Bhd and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK).
Ta Ann's target price of RM8.55 compares with its market price of RM5.68 (Oct 20), giving it the highest potential upside among the six plantation companies assessed.

SD Guthrie follows with a target price of RM7.81, representing a 36.5 per cent upside from RM5.72 (Oct 20), while Genting Plantations has a target price of RM6.84, implying a 34.1 per cent gain from RM5.10 (Oct 20), the firm said in a recent note.
It said Sarawak Plantation offers a potential upside of 27.9 per cent, with a target price of RM5.59 against its price of RM4.37 (Oct 20).

Among the larger plantation counters, KLK has a target price of RM23.86, suggesting an 18.4 per cent upside from RM20.16 (Oct 20), while IOI Corp has a target price of RM5.06, representing a 12.4 per cent gain from RM4.50 (Oct 20).
The preference for selected plantation stocks comes as investors weigh earnings growth and dividend income against commodity-price volatility, production costs and changing export dynamics.

Based on financial forecasts, PublicInvest analyst Chong Hoe Leong said Ta Ann offers the highest projected dividend yield among the six companies at 8.8 per cent for both financial years 2026 and 2027. Sarawak Plantation follows at 6.9 per cent, while Genting Plantations offers 5.8 per cent.

Ta Ann's appeal is further supported by its earnings outlook. Its earnings per share (EPS) are forecast to rise from 63.3 sen in 2026 to 66.1 sen in 2027, while its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is expected to decline from nine times to 8.6 times.

Sarawak Plantation is also expected to deliver earnings growth, with EPS projected to increase from 43.1 sen in 2026 to 46.6 sen in 2027. Its forward P/E ratio is forecast to ease from 10.1 times to 9.4 times, alongside a projected dividend yield of 6.9 per cent.
Its return on equity (ROE) is expected to improve from 13.9 per cent in 2026 to 14.3 per cent in 2027, placing it among the stronger performers in the group.
Genting Plantations, meanwhile, is forecast to record EPS of 46.9 sen in 2026 and 47.1 sen in 2027, with its forward P/E ratio remaining relatively stable at 10.9 times and 10.8 times, respectively.

The outlook is less straightforward for SD Guthrie, despite its substantial implied share-price upside. Its EPS is projected to decline from 42.7 sen in 2026 to 39 sen in 2027, representing a fall of 8.6 per cent, while its forward P/E ratio is expected to rise from 13.4 times to 14.7 times. Its dividend yield is also forecast to moderate from 3.8 per cent to 3.5 per cent.

For IOI Corp, EPS is expected to rise from 25.1 sen in 2026 to 26.2 sen in 2027, while its forward P/E ratio declines from 17.9 times to 17.2 times. Its dividend yield is projected to edge up from 2.8 per cent to 2.9 per cent.

KLK is similarly expected to post moderate earnings growth, with EPS rising from RM1.162 to RM1.204 over the same period. Its forward P/E ratio is forecast to ease from 17.3 times to 16.7 times, while its dividend yield remains at 3 per cent.
Ta Ann also leads the group in projected ROE, at 15.6 per cent in 2026 and 15.3 per cent in 2027, followed by Sarawak Plantation at 13.9 per cent and 14.3 per cent, respectively.

The valuations suggest that Ta Ann and Sarawak Plantation offer a combination of income and earnings growth, while the target-price upside at SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations may appeal to investors seeking capital appreciation.

However, target prices are estimates rather than guaranteed returns, and the sector's performance will remain sensitive to crude palm oil prices, fresh fruit bunch production, operating costs and export competitiveness.
98c31e8a9bc73ac7: TIRANA: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday vowed a tougher line against anti-government protesters, saying that fines would be introduced for violent demonstrations, as hundreds of people marched again in the capital.
Albania has been wracked by months of anti-government protests that in recent days have deteriorated into pitched battles between the security forces and protesters.

Rama said a new law would be released this week allowing for fines of more than US$550 for "anyone who chooses to remain in a crowd" that is carrying out acts of violence or looting in a public space, or "concealing their identity".
In a speech broadcast on social media, he said the clampdown would apply to any type of gathering "when it results in property damage".
The new law would give police the powers to restrict "gatherings" in certain cases if there was a risk of violence, Rama said.
"Anyone demanding my resignation is mistaken if they think it can be forced or imposed in any way, but I do not believe that everything they are saying and demanding is wrong," he added.
Rama's statement came as several hundred people in the capital staged a fresh protest outside his offices, with protesters shrugging off the threat of fines.
"Why do parents have to pay for the acts of their children while the prime minister isn't responsible for the acts of his government," a pensioner who declined to give her name told AFP.
Several clashes between demonstrtors and police flared on Sunday evening.
Opposition leader and fierce Rama rival Sali Berisha, head of the Democratic Party, said people would not accept the new government measures, his party said in a press release.
"We will stand firmly against them" and "respond tooth for tooth" to Rama "to give him what he deserves", Berisha told an online exchange with the public.

The new law also allows for compensation for small companies affected by protests and action against those who "encourage, organise or coordinate the participation of minor school children in rallies".
Teachers have backed high school students who have taken part in the protests this year.
In recent protests, demonstrators have attacked the education ministry and other official buildings, complaining about corruption and demanding better conditions for students and Rama's resignation.
Police said after Saturday's protests that 23 people had been formally arrested, 13 others face legal proceedings and 30 people were "wanted".
